intro.title: Number of Connected Components
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a function that counts the number of connected components in an undirected graph. You will learn to use Depth-First Search (DFS) to traverse and explore each component. The main technologies involved are JavaScript arrays, objects for adjacency lists, and recursion or iteration for DFS. This will help you understand fundamental graph algorithms and how to apply them to solve connectivity problems.
intro.usecase: The algorithm for counting connected components is a foundational pattern for analyzing networks and relationships in real-world data. Developers use it in social networks to identify distinct friend groups, in infrastructure monitoring to detect isolated server clusters after an outage, and in image processing to segment distinct objects. For example, a network health dashboard might use this to visually group connected servers into components, helping engineers quickly assess system resilience and pinpoint disconnected segments.
